footage.what: Still screenshots and gameplay footage of Spore Creature Creator 2D showing the creature editor (parts palette, spine/body manipulation, creature naming) and the totem-pole training minigame (Level 1 completion, projectile deflection with a green targeting ring).

Continuous gameplay capture of Spore Creature Creator 2D from the title screen ('Start' button), camera pan down to a hatching egg on a pedestal, spine/vertebra manipulation tutorial, color palette selection, and attaching mouths/eyes from the parts menu.

rules.rule: The game begins on a title screen featuring the 'Presented By Spore Hero / Spore Creature Creator 2D' logo over a starry night sky with a crescent moon and a 'Start' button. Clicking 'Start' pans the camera vertically down through clouds into a daytime forest clearing with a circular stone pedestal.
On the pedestal, a spotted egg appears, rocks back and forth, cracks, and hatches into an initial vertical cyan/green blob (the base spine/torso) to begin creature creation.
The game has two primary modes: 'Build/Paint' (Creature Editor) and 'Play/Train' (Totem Minigame), toggled via top-center circular mode buttons or bottom bar navigation.
The entire game (both editor and minigame) is rendered from a fixed 2D side-view (profile) perspective with layered 2D background art.

Clicking the creature's body reveals a segmented spine with numbered vertebrae (1 to 6+) and directional arrows at the top and bottom. The player drags vertebrae and arrows to bend, curve, and resize the torso ('Basic Building: Drag to manipulate vertebra and spine').

In 'Build' mode (hammer icon at top-center), a left-hand vertical panel displays creature parts in a 3-column grid (up to 6 rows per page, 18 parts per page) with pagination controls at the bottom (e.g., '1/3', '1/2') and 7 category tabs along the top of the panel: Mouths, Senses (eyes/ears/noses), Limbs/Arms, Legs/Feet, Graspers/Hands, Weapons/Horns/Spikes, and Details/Accessories.

Parts are dragged from the left palette onto the 2D creature body. There is no DNA budget or currency cost shown; instead, a 10-dot meter in the top-right corner tracks complexity or part count (dots fill in white as parts are added).
rules.evidence: Video 1 21:35, 21:44 (narrator notes no DNA limitations); Video 2 18:30, 18:41-18:48

rules.rule: Clicking the top-center Paintbrush icon switches to 'Paint' mode, opening a right-hand panel ('Base') with a 3x5 grid of 15 color swatches. Holding the left mouse button on a swatch displays additional color/detail choices ('Click and hold left mouse button to display more color choices'). Selecting a swatch immediately recolors the creature's body and attached parts.

The bottom bar of the editor contains: a 'Spore Hero' logo link (left), a grid/gallery icon, a creature/play icon, a central text input box ('Choose Your Name' where players type names like 'Tecnomon' or 'feroz escorpion'), Undo/Redo curved arrows, a Reset/Clear icon, and a Save/Shopping cart icon (right).

In the training minigame, the player's 2D creature stands on the right side of a stone platform in a tribal/jungle arena. On the left side sits a wheeled wooden cart carrying a stack of three colorful tiki/totem pole heads (purple bottom, teal middle, yellow/horned top).

The totem pole heads shoot small patterned orbs/projectiles across the screen toward the creature. A green circular target reticle appears over the creature's weapon/mouth part; the player clicks (or positions the cursor and clicks) when the orb enters the green ring to strike/deflect it.

The top UI bar in the minigame displays the current level on the left ('Level 1'), a segmented progress bar in the center with a flag icon below it showing a level number (e.g., '1', '2', '3'), and a numeric score on the right (e.g., '0', '90'). Filling the progress bar triggers a 'Level Completed - Click To Continue' overlay.

The bottom bar of the minigame features Pause ('||') and Play/Fast-forward ('>>') buttons on the left, the creature's name in a banner in the center, and a Return/Replay arrow and Help ('?') button on the right. A speaker mute toggle sits in the top-right corner across all screens.
Completing levels in the totem minigame likely unlocks additional part categories or pages in the creature editor, or advances the flag tier.

Original game audio is not audible in either clip (covered by narrator voiceovers and background music), though a speaker mute icon in the top-right corner confirms the game had sound effects and/or music.
